absaetze.t: Mardi 24 novembre, les eurodéputés ont largement adopté une loi visant à protéger les producteurs d'aliments biologiques. Les normes pour afficher l'Eurofeuille sur un produit seront renforcées pour les pays tiers, avec des exceptions pour les petits producteurs, ce qui présente des limites pour plusieurs eurodéputés.

Une avancée pour l'agriculture biologique ? Mardi 24 novembre, les députés européens ont adopté de nouvelles mesures qui visent à renforcer la protection des producteurs de produits biologiques. Cette révision ciblée du règlement européen sur la production biologique a été largement adoptée (486 voix pour, 39 voix contre et 140 abstentions).

Le texte présente plusieurs dispositions pour protéger les producteurs, notamment de la concurrence déloyale. Concrètement, les pays avec lesquels l'UE a un accord d'équivalence "ne peuvent utiliser le logo de production biologique de l’UE dans leur étiquetage, leur présentation et leur publicité que s’ils sont conformes à des normes équivalentes et, le cas échéant, répondent à des exigences supplémentaires en matière de production et de contrôle de ceux produits dans l’UE", précise le texte. Les produits concernés pourront en revanche continuer à utiliser le logo biologique de leur pays d'origine.
Renforcer la confiance des consommateurs

"Mon objectif est de doter ce secteur vital d’un cadre réglementaire stable, cohérent et prévisible. Qui simplifie les exigences existantes tout en évitant les révisions législatives répétées après son introduction", a déclaré la rapporteure du texte, Camilla Laureti, députée italienne (Socialistes & Démocrates).

Les produits importés de pays tiers dont les normes biologiques sont reconnues comme équivalentes à celles de l'UE ne pourront afficher l'Eurofeuille qu'à condition de respecter également certaines exigences européennes en matière de production et de contrôle. Cette évolution fait suite à un arrêt de la Cour de justice de l'Union européenne du 4 octobre 2024, qui a remis en cause l'utilisation du logo bio européen pour certains produits importés dans le cadre d'accords d'équivalence.

Le texte prolonge jusqu'au 31 décembre 2036 la reconnaissance d'équivalence accordée à 11 pays tiers, parmi lesquels l'Argentine, la Nouvelle-Zélande et les États-Unis. Il doit désormais être formellement approuvé par le Conseil avant d'entrer en vigueur.
Limiter les contraintes pour les petits producteurs

Le Parlement et le Conseil ont par ailleurs écarté la proposition de la Commission visant à autoriser l'utilisation du label biologique de l'UE sur les produits contenant moins de 5 % d'ingrédients provenant de pays tiers qui ne satisfont pas aux critères supplémentaires.

Pour éviter que ces nouvelles règles ne constituent une charge excessive pour les petits producteurs, les négociateurs ont prévu des exemptions pour les petites entreprises qui vendent directement aux consommateurs. Elles pourront être dispensées des procédures de certification biologique "à condition qu’elles vendent jusqu’à 10 000 kg par an et que leur chiffre d’affaires annuel soit inférieur à 40 000 euros".

Ces chiffres ont par ailleurs été doublés pendant les négociations pour permettre à un plus grand nombre de petits producteurs d’en bénéficier. "Il est toujours plus compliqué de se conformer aux normes pour les plus petits producteurs, mais pensons au rôle qu'ils jouent dans l'agriculture durable et dans l'écologie, il est important de les appuyer et de les soutenir", a insisté Camilla Laureti. À l'inverse, Arash Saeidi, député de La France insoumise et rapporteur fictif sur ce texte, estime que le relèvement de ces seuils pourrait fragiliser la confiance des consommateurs dans le bio. "Je crains qu'avec cette augmentation du seuil, ces mesures ne visent plus seulement les producteurs qui vendent en direct, et que des petites structures soient également incluses", explique-t-il à Toute l'Europe. Selon lui, le contrôle du respect des normes biologiques pourrait également s'avérer plus difficile, en particulier dans les pays tiers. "Le secteur est déjà en difficulté, je m'inquiète du signal que l'on donne sur le bio", regrette-t-il.
Un cadre français déjà plus exigeant sur certains aspects

Marie Toussaint, eurodéputée et vice-présidente du groupe des Verts/ALE, voit dans ce texte une avancée pour la quasi-totalité des États membres, mais appelle à une vigilance particulière dans le cas de la France. "On a des spécificités nationales, la France a des soutiens au bio notamment dans la restauration collective, qui sont un peu meilleurs que ce qu'il y a dans ce texte, c'est donc à la fois une vraie avancée pour les autres États de l'UE mais on a une vigilance particulière pour la France", a-t-elle confié à Toute l'Europe. Une préoccupation partagée, sous un autre angle, par Arash Saeidi : "Cela peut inciter les Français à faire moins bien, étant donné qu'ils ne seront pas soumis aux mêmes contraintes que les autres".

La France dispose en effet de mesures nationales de soutien à l'agriculture biologique dans des domaines qui ne sont pas couverts par cette révision, notamment en matière d'approvisionnement de la restauration collective. La loi EGalim impose ainsi qu'au moins 20 % de la valeur des achats de denrées alimentaires dans les établissements concernés soient constitués de produits issus de l'agriculture biologique ou en conversion. Cette obligation ne trouve pas d'équivalent dans la révision européenne, essentiellement axée sur les règles de production, de certification, d'étiquetage et d'importation.
Ces réserves expliquent l'abstention des eurodéputés écologistes français, alors que la majorité des membres de leur groupe au Parlement européen s'est prononcée en faveur du texte.

Par ailleurs, le texte européen aborde la lutte contre les contaminations croisées entre cultures biologiques et conventionnelles. Afin de les limiter, la Commission européenne devra publier, à partir du 31 décembre 2031, des orientations sur les bonnes pratiques à mettre en œuvre.

items.titel: ‘Null and void’: EU rejects Libya-Turkey pact that could allow oil drilling in Greek waters
items.anriss: The EU has rejected as “null and void” a controversial maritime pact between Turkey and Libya that is bitterly opposed by Greece and could pave the way for Turkish oil and gas exploration close to Crete.

absaetze.t: The EU has rejected as “null and void” a controversial maritime pact between Turkey and Libya that is bitterly opposed by Greece and could pave the way for Turkish oil and gas exploration close to Crete.

The memorandum proposes a maritime corridor across the eastern Mediterranean from north-east Libya to south-west Turkey, and would create an avenue for Turkey and Libya to conduct potentially lucrative joint gas exploration and drilling operations.

Greece argues, with the support of both the EU and United Nations, that the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) breaches Greek sovereignty over waters surrounding the island of Crete and its Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ).

The EU’s Mediterranean commissioner Dubravka Šuica told MEPs in Strasbourg on Tuesday (24 November) that the memorandum “does not comply with the law of the society…it is null and void”, adding that the EU Commission “reiterates full solidarity with Greece and Cyprus.”
The commission had “consistently reflected these concerns to Turkey”, she said.

The maritime deal was originally agreed between Turkey and the Tripoli based Government of National Accord, which has been recognised as Libya’s government by the EU and most of the international community.
But it was opposed by general Khalifa Haftar, the leader of the Libyan National Army, which has operated a rival administration in eastern Libya.
But in October, the Tobruk-based House of Representatives, backed in Haftar, approved the memorandum, paving the way for Turkish firms to start oil and gas exploration.

items.titel: MEPs still split over ending Hungary’s Article 7 sanctions procedure, but Magyar’s reforms win praise
items.anriss: The centre-right European People’s Party (EPP), the European Parliament’s largest group, says Hungary is no longer breaching EU core values and is pushing to end the ‘Article 7’ sanctions proceedings – but other groups warn the job isn’t …

absaetze.t: The centre-right European People’s Party (EPP), the European Parliament’s largest group, says Hungary is no longer breaching EU core values and is pushing to end the ‘Article 7’ sanctions proceedings – but other groups warn the job isn’t finished, setting up a tight December vote to close the file.

Acknowledging that “years of damage cannot be undone in just six months,” centre-right Swedish MEP Tomas Tobé (EPP) welcomed the progress since Péter Magyar’s centre-right government won the parliamentary elections in April, ending 16 years of Viktor Orbán’s illiberal rule.
“Progress must be recognised,” he said.
So did the commission earlier this year, when billions of euros in frozen EU cohesion and recovery funds for Hungary were partially unblocked following rule-of-law and anti-corruption reforms.
“Is everything perfect? Of course not, but the political will is there,” also said Belgian liberal MEP and former prime minister Sophie Wilmès during the debate.

“We kept banging against the same wall: Viktor Orbán. In April, Hungarians themselves broke down this wall,” she said, adding that, in response, the EU Parliament should send Hungarians a “positive signal of encouragement.”
But a Polish centre-left MEP, Krzysztof Śmiszek, said that while the current reforms were “important,” they were not enough to say there was no “threat to rule of law.”
German Green MEP Daniel Freund has also warned against closing the EU’s rule-of-law procedure just yet, warning that Hungary still fails to comply with an EU asylum ruling.

Magyar’s new government has already made "extraordinary progress ", but "many tasks still lie ahead [to uphold EU values],” also said Tineke Strik, a Green MEP leading the parliament’s work on Hungary rule of law.
“We owe it to Hungarian people to be diligent in our assessment”, she added.

In 2018, the European Parliament triggered the EU treaty's Article 7 procedure against Hungary over serious rule of law breaches, which could have ultimately resulted in sanctions such as suspending Hungary’s voting rights in the Council.

But this never happened – neither to Hungary nor to Poland, the only two countries which have ever been under the Article 7 procedure, given the need for unanimous support and amid fears of retaliation by other rightwing governments.

To formally end the Article 7 procedure, MEPs must vote to withdraw it, and that decision requires a two-thirds majority, meaning at least 480 of the parliament's 719 lawmakers, before the council, representing member states, can close the file.

Meanwhile, despite rule-of-law breaches and the dismantling of democratic institutions in Hungary, Orbán’s Fidesz party was a member of the EPP group until 2021, which triggered criticism from left-wing MEPs during Tuesday’s debate in Strasbourg.

items.titel: US-Medienberichte: Trump plant wohl neue Zölle
items.anriss: Die US-Regierung bereitet offenbar neue Zölle gegenüber China, der EU und weiteren Ländern vor. Der Schritt erfolgt, nachdem die Zölle vom Supreme Court als illegal eingestuft wurden.[ mehr ]

absaetze.t: Die US-Regierung bereitet offenbar neue Zölle gegenüber China, der EU und weiteren Ländern vor. Der Schritt erfolgt, nachdem die Zölle vom Supreme Court als illegal eingestuft wurden.

Die Trump-Regierung wird voraussichtlich in Kürze Pläne zur Erhöhung der Zölle gegenüber China, der Europäischen Union und 14 weiteren Volkswirtschaften bekannt geben. Das berichten zwei mit der Angelegenheit vertraute Personen der Nachrichtenagentur AP. Über die Pläne hatten Bloomberg, Reuters und das Wall Street Journal bereits zuvor berichtet.

Das Büro des US-Handelsbeauftragten (USTR) wird voraussichtlich in den kommenden Tagen die Ergebnisse einer monatelangen Zolluntersuchung zu den Industriesubventionen der 16 Volkswirtschaften veröffentlichen. Das sagten die Quellen, die unter der Bedingung der Anonymität sprachen, der AP.
Sie betonten, dass sich der Zeitpunkt für die Einführung der Zölle noch ändern könnte. Das Weiße Haus und das USTR reagierten demnach nicht auf Anfragen nach einer Stellungnahme.
Zoll-Konflikt zwischen USA und EU

Die Pläne für die neuen Zölle sind Teil der Bemühungen, die von der US-Regierung im vergangenen Jahr festgelegten, umfassenderen Zölle zu ersetzen, die anschließend vom Supreme Court für verfassungswidrig erklärt wurden.

Bei den Ländern könnte es sich handeln um China, Indien, Japan, Südkorea, Mexiko, Vietnam, Taiwan, Thailand, Malaysia, Indonesien, die Schweiz, Norwegen, Singapur, Bangladesch und Kambodscha sowie die Europäische Union.

Die Zölle seien eine Reaktion auf die - nach Auffassung des Weißen Hauses - durch Subventionen angekurbelte, übermäßige Produktionsleistung in diesen Ländern, die zu einer Flut von Waren zu niedrigeren Preisen geführt habe, und die damit die amerikanischen Unternehmen unterbieten.

Die Zölle stellen einen zweiten Schritt in den Bemühungen der US-Regierung dar, die im April 2025 angekündigten Zölle zu ersetzen, die der Oberste Gerichtshof im Februar für verfassungswidrig erklärt hatte.

Das Weiße Haus hatte im Juli gegen 60 Handelspartner Zölle in Höhe von 10 bis 12,5 Prozent verhängt und ihnen vorgeworfen, Verbote für durch Zwangsarbeit hergestellte Waren nicht ausreichend durchgesetzt zu haben.

items.titel: Keine schnelle Lösung bei Gewalt gegen Frauen
items.anriss: Der heutige Orange Day steht für eine Zukunft ohne Gewalt gegen Frauen. Doch die Realität sieht anders aus. Strafverschärfungen und Gesetzesänderungen sind angestoßen, aber schnelle Lösungen sind nicht in Sicht. Von A. Lagmöller. [ mehr ]

absaetze.t: Orange Day Mehr Gewalt gegen Frauen - keine schnelle Lösung in Sicht

Der heutige Orange Day steht für eine Zukunft ohne Gewalt gegen Frauen. Doch die Realität sieht anders aus. Strafverschärfungen und Gesetzesänderungen sind angestoßen, aber schnelle Lösungen sind nicht in Sicht.

"Frau sein, das kann heißen, dass die eigene sexuelle Selbstbestimmung brutal missachtet wird und Frau zu sein, das kann heißen, dass man wegen seines Geschlechtes beleidigt und herabgewürdigt wird im digitalen Raum aber eben auch auf Straßen und Plätzen und in den eigenen vier Wänden."

So beschreibt Bundesjustizministerin Stefanie Hubig die Gegenwart für viele Frauen in Deutschland. Die Zukunft soll aber orange sein. Die Farbe symbolisiert den internationalen Tag zur Beseitigung von Gewalt gegen Frauen.
Steigende Zahlen bei Gewalt gegen Frauen

Im Moment ist dieses Ziel allerdings in weiter Ferne. Die Bundesregierung hat in Berlin Zahlen zu häuslicher Gewalt und zu geschlechtsspezifischer Gewalt gegen Frauen vorgestellt. Bundesinnenminister Alexander Dobrindt nannte die Zahlen zutiefst schockierend. "Wir verzeichnen steigende Opferzahlen in allen Bereichen. Hinter diesen oftmals nüchternen statistischen Zahlen stehen schlimmste Erlebnisse, schmerzhafteste Erinnerungen."
Konkret geht es um mehr als 280.000 Opfer von häuslicher Gewalt, 70 Prozent davon Frauen und Mädchen. Mehr als 54.000 Frauen und Mädchen wurden Opfer von Sexualstraftaten.

Der Großteil der Fälle würden aber gar nicht erfasst. "95 Prozent der Taten liegen im Dunkelfeld", sagt Hubig im Interview mit den tagesthemen. Man müsse dringend alles dafür tun und Unterstützung geben, "dass Menschen dann den Weg der Anzeige gehen und des Strafverfahrens."
Was die Bundesregierung unternimmt

Die Bundesregierung bleibt nicht untätig. Partnerschaftsgewalt soll in Zukunft zwingend eine Rolle spielen, wenn es am Familiengericht um das Sorge- oder Umgangsrecht für das gemeinsame Kind geht. Gewalttäter können bald zum Tragen einer elektronischen Fußfessel verpflichtet werden.

Und an vielen Stellen soll das Strafgesetzbuch geändert werden. Femizide, also wenn zum Beispiel ein Mann seine Ex-Partnerin aus Eifersucht tötet, sollen künftig stets als Morde bestraft werden. Und in Zukunft soll es auch dann eine Vergewaltigung sein, wenn die Frau nicht ausdrücklich "Nein" sagt, etwa weil sie sich in einer Schockstarre befindet.
Härtere Strafen haben "nur geringe abschreckende Wirkung"

Aber schrecken Strafverschärfungen ab? Christine Morgenstern, Professorin für Kriminologie an der Universität Bochum, ist skeptisch: "Wir gehen davon aus, dass Strafnormen keine oder nur eine sehr geringe abschreckende Wirkung haben, auch in diesem Bereich der sexualisierten Gewalt oder Gewalt gegen Frauen."

Was helfen könnte? Morgenstern verweist auf das Gewalthilfegesetz, das schon Anfang vergangenen Jahres verabschiedet wurde. Danach soll jede Frau einen kostenlosen Rechtsanspruch auf Schutz und Beratung haben - aber erst ab 2032. Morgenstern fände es glaubwürdiger, wenn bestimmte Dinge aus dem Gewalthilfegesetz jetzt schon umgesetzt würden, wenn Täterarbeit umgesetzt würde und man nicht nur konkret ist mit Änderung im Strafgesetzbuch, sondern auch mit Vorschlägen wie einem großen Präventionsprogramm an Schulen.
Prävention kostet Geld

Die Kehrseite: Um dem Anspruch aus dem Gewalthilfegesetz gerecht zu werden, müssen Bund und Länder ausreichend Schutz, Beratung und Unterstützung anbieten - und finanzieren. Derzeit fehlen aber noch 12.000 Plätze in Frauenhäusern.

Geld spielt aber auch für die einzelne Frau eine Rolle, die sich aus einer gewalttätigen Beziehung befreien möchte, sagt Kathrin Gebel, frauenpolitische Sprecherin der Linken im Bundestag. Die ökonomische Eigenständigkeit von Frauen habe in der Debatte bisher nicht so eine große Rolle gespielt. "70 Prozent aller Frauen können langfristig nicht ihr Kind und sich selbst versorgen und das macht sie extrem vulnerabel für Gewaltbetroffenheit."

Bis zur "orangen Zukunft" ist es noch ein langer Weg. Im Bundestag hat es der Orange Day schon jetzt auf die Agenda geschafft: Für die Opfer von Femiziden hat Bundestagspräsidentin Julia Klöckner einen Schweigemoment eingeplant.

items.titel: Libye: deux militaires libyens morts des suites des attaques ukrainiennes contre des navires russes à Benghazi
items.anriss: Deux militaires libyens ont succombé à leurs blessures à la suite des attaques contre des navires russes à Benghazi, le 22 novembre, revendiquées par l'Ukraine, ont annoncé dans la nuit de mardi à mercredi les autorités de l'Est libyen.

absaetze.t: Deux militaires libyens ont succombé à leurs blessures à la suite des attaques contre des navires russes à Benghazi, le 22 novembre, revendiquées par l'Ukraine, ont annoncé dans la nuit de mardi à mercredi les autorités de l'Est libyen.
2 min Temps de lecture

« C'est avec une profonde tristesse et une grande fierté que je rends aujourd'hui hommage à deux héros de nos forces navales », a déclaré sur Facebook Saddam Haftar, fils du maréchal Khalifa Haftar et commandant en chef adjoint des Forces armées arabes libyennes. Ils sont « tombés en martyrs des suites des blessures subies dans l'exercice de leur devoir national lors de l'attaque criminelle visant la base navale de Benghazi », a-t-il ajouté.

Dans un communiqué distinct, le chef du gouvernement de l'Est, Oussama Hamad, a présenté ses condoléances au commandement général des Forces armées arabes libyennes. Il a précisé que les deux hommes étaient décédés « à la suite de leurs blessures lors de l'agression ukrainienne perfide contre le port de Benghazi ».
Les autorités libyennes demandent des explications

Le président ukrainien, Volodymyr Zelensky, a revendiqué les attaques menées dimanche près de Benghazi, grande ville de l'Est libyen, lors desquelles deux navires russes ont été pris pour cible, selon Kiev. Il a salué une « opération exemplaire en réponse à la guerre russe ».

Le gouvernement libyen d'unité nationale, basé à Tripoli, a réclamé des explications à Kiev, tandis que l'exécutif rival de l'Est a demandé une enquête internationale sur une présumée présence militaire ukrainienne en Libye.

La Libye est divisée entre un gouvernement reconnu par l'ONU à Tripoli et une administration parallèle dans l'est du pays, soutenue par le maréchal Haftar. Le camp Haftar entretient depuis plusieurs années des liens militaires et stratégiques étroits avec la Russie.
La Mission d'appui des Nations unies en Libye (Manul) avait elle aussi dénoncé les attaques, réclamant une enquête indépendante et appelant au respect de la souveraineté libyenne.

items.titel: Présidentielle 2027: Édouard Philippe marque ses différences avec David Lisnard
items.anriss: Édouard Philippe s'est rendu mardi 24 novembre au Salon des maires, organisé porte de Versailles, à Paris. Le candidat Horizons à la présidentielle de 2027 entend afficher son intérêt pour les élus locaux, mais aussi marquer ses …

absaetze.t: Édouard Philippe s'est rendu mardi 24 novembre au Salon des maires, organisé porte de Versailles, à Paris. Le candidat Horizons à la présidentielle de 2027 entend afficher son intérêt pour les élus locaux, mais aussi marquer ses différences avec son concurrent David Lisnard, maire de Cannes et candidat à sa réélection à la tête de l'Association des maires de France (AMF).
2 min Temps de lecture

Dans les travées du Congrès des maires de France, Édouard Philippe joue la décontraction. Le maire du Havre termine une gaufre, son dessert du déjeuner, tout en serrant des mains. Le candidat Horizons à la présidentielle de 2027 veut montrer que tout va bien dans sa campagne, alors que David Lisnard est désormais à son niveau dans les sondages.

Édouard Philippe entend bien disputer le terrain à son concurrent, également candidat à la présidentielle sous les couleurs de Nouvelle Énergie. Il se montre même beau joueur à l'occasion du scrutin pour la présidence de l'AMF, où David Lisnard brigue un nouveau mandat. « Alors j'ai déjà voté, j'ai voté pour David Lisnard parce que c'est un bon président des maires », a-t-il déclaré.

Mais ce compliment est aussitôt suivi d'un tacle contre son rival : « Je n'ai aucun problème à dire pour qui je vote. J'ai compris qu'il avait un petit peu plus de mal à dire pour qui il voterait dans l'hypothèse d'un second tour entre Madame Le Pen et moi. Ça prouve qu'on peut aimer les tronçonneuses et pas savoir trancher. » Une allusion au programme du maire de Cannes, qui prévoit notamment la suppression de 400 000 postes de fonctionnaires.
Des divergences sur la droite et le centre

Pour Édouard Philippe, l'heure est désormais à la mise en avant des différences politiques avec David Lisnard, notamment sur la stratégie à adopter pour la présidentielle. « Monsieur Lisnard a indiqué que l'objectif de cette primaire, c'était d'éliminer le centre. Mais moi, ce n'est pas du tout ma stratégie. Mon objectif, c'est de rassembler la droite et le centre », a affirmé le candidat Horizons.

Dans l'entourage du maire du Havre, certains évoquent « Docteur David et Mister Lisnard » pour pointer les ambiguïtés du maire de Cannes, notamment dans ses relations avec l'extrême droite. Une question de valeurs sur laquelle Édouard Philippe entend marquer sa différence. « Moi, j'ai toujours dit que je ne travaillerai jamais avec la droite extrême, jamais », a-t-il insisté. L'ancien Premier ministre durcit ainsi le ton pour souligner les enjeux de son duel avec David Lisnard dans la course à la présidentielle de 2027.

L'actualité politique d'Édouard Philippe se heurte aussi à son actualité judiciaire : le candidat est visé par une enquête, ouverte à la suite d'un signalement à la justice pour détournement de fonds publics auprès du parquet du Havre. Le maire de la ville a dénoncé, à ce sujet, une « vendetta judiciaire ».

items.titel: Lynx KF41 Fighting Vehicles, Newly Arrived In Ukraine, Will Take On Counter-Drone Mission
items.anriss: Ukraine has finally received its first batch of Lynx KF41 Infantry Fighting Vehicles from Germany. While the role of armor in the Ukraine war has been drastically diminished due to the proliferation of drone threats, it’s somewhat ironic …

absaetze.t: Ukraine has finally received its first batch of Lynx KF41 Infantry Fighting Vehicles from Germany. While the role of armor in the Ukraine war has been drastically diminished due to the proliferation of drone threats, it’s somewhat ironic that the unit operating the Lynx said one of its main tasks will be to shoot down Russian drones.

Ukraine’s 18th Army Corps announced on Telegram Tuesday that the 21st Separate Mechanized Brigade has taken delivery of the Lynx vehicles under a deal with the German arms maker Rheinmetall that was confirmed in January. Hungary was the first country to receive the Lynx from Germany and later built their own. Italy and Romania are also on the docket to get Lynx, and the U.S. is currently evaluating it to replace the Bradley.
The Counter-Drone Mission
In the version provided to Ukraine, the Lynx’s two-person Lance turret is equipped with a 30mm autocannon and it also features a 12.7mm machine gun in a remote weapon station.

The autocannon fires Rheinmetall’s Advanced Hit Efficiency And Destruction (AHEAD) programmable airburst round that releases a cloud of shrapnel just ahead of a target, drastically increasing the probability of a kill and making it better suited to tackling low-flying smaller air threats like drones, rockets, and mortar projectiles, although it needs special sensors to shoot down the latter two. As well as increasing the speed of engagements and boosting lethality, airburst rounds also significantly reduce the risk of collateral damage on the ground as the rounds detonate at a prescribed distance. The typical effective range of the 30mm cannon is around 1.8 miles.
In a video published by the brigade, soldiers explained how Lynx will be used in a counter-drone role.

“The heart, so to speak, of the vehicle is the main computer,” one of the troops stated in the video, according to a machine translation. “The computer runs a program that determines at what distance from the target—target after target—the shell will detonate. Similarly, the number of shells fired—say, 100—is programmed to detonate upon hitting this target. We’ll also use this vehicle to combat enemy UAVs.”
“And we fire a five-round salvo at the target,” another soldier proffered. “The shells explode in front of the target, creating a cloud of shrapnel.”
To acquire targets like drones, the Lynx uses its Lance 2 turret, which is a multi-role system with a counter-drone upgrade, according to the company.

While it would be able to use its optics to engage aerial targets, detecting them in the first place and locking onto them is another matter. There is no visible radar system on the vehicle. It would likely need to rely on passive sensors, which have limited effectiveness, and possibly being cued by external systems, for detection. Beyond that, the crew would visually have to acquire threats and try to engage them, which can be challenging to say the least, especially when buried inside an armored vehicle and looking through narrow optical sensor feeds. This does not mean it can’t be effective in shooting down drones in some circumstances, but it is not an optimized air defense system for that purpose with its own active sensors.

The brigade’s interest in using the Lynx in a counter drone role comes as Ukraine continues to struggle against waves of Russian uncrewed aerial threats of many kinds, from small FPV and fiber optic drones to jet-powered one way attack drones.
Armor Still Has A Role

As we noted at the top of this story, both Ukraine and Russia have reduced their reliance on armor, especially for maneuver, due to threats from drones, loitering munitions, and advanced anti-tank weapons.

However, recent Ukrainian offensives showed that armor is still being employed effectively. This is done in concert with aerial drones used to attack enemy troop positions, uncrewed ground vehicles used to clear mines, and aerial drones used as escorts covering armor movements. Artillery can also be employed as part of these combined arms operations. In the case of Operation Vivaldi in Ukraine’s eastern region of Donetsk, armor punched through weakened Russian lines using these tactics.

In a battle in the northeastern Kharkiv region last month, Ukrainian forces employed a tank and a U.S.-made Bradley Fighting Vehicle – heavily covered in steel cope caging – to advance into Russian-held territory while covered by aerial drones. As we noted earlier, a variant of the Lynx is on a shortlist to replace the Bradley in the U.S. Army.

In addition to its counter drone role, the 21st Separate Mechanized Brigade will use the Lynx to transport troops and employ the 30mm autocannon to engage Russian infantry and light armored vehicles. AHEAD ammo is also useful for that, being capable of detonating behind cover, for instance.

The KF41 has a standard crew of three as well as provisions to transport a squad of up to eight infantry. As well as the standard attributes of mobility and firepower, the design of the Lynx focuses on a high level of protection to defend against certain anti-armor weapons, medium-caliber ammunition, artillery shrapnel, and bomb blasts.
There is also the option to add active protection systems if specified by the customer.
The vehicle can reach speeds of up to 50 miles per hour.

“Among its main advantages are its high level of protection, mobility, spacious turret and troop compartment, and effective weaponry,” the 18th Army Corps said of the Lynx. “The modern fire control system and gun with programmable ammunition allow for the effective engagement of a variety of ground and air targets on the battlefield.”
Factory Fresh
Unlike the vast majority of armored vehicles donated to Ukraine, the KF41s received by the brigade are new.

“The vehicles came from Germany—straight from the factory,” one of the soldiers in the video pointed out. “Some of them had only 10 kilometers on the odometer. None of the vehicles had ever been used before; this was their first time.”
Soldiers from the brigade spent six weeks in Germany to learn how to operate the vehicles.
“The training was very intensive,” one of the soldiers recalled. Mechanics and drivers “trained every day from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Commanders and gunners trained separately.”

Troops from the brigade “went through the theory and practical training on these vehicles,” the soldier added. “At the training ground, there were firing exercises, night patrols, and night firing from these vehicles. We were at the training ground…under fire.”
The Lynx is not the first foreign fighting vehicle to debut with the 21st Separate Mechanized Brigade. In 2023, the unit became the first to operate the Swedish-made CV90 Infantry Fighting Vehicles.
At the time the sole Ukrainian operator of the CV90s, the brigade initially used the vehicles for combat in the eastern Bakhmut and northeastern Kupyansk sectors, according to the Kyiv Post.
Trial Run

Rhinemetall has a lot riding on how the Lynx performs in Ukraine. The company developed the vehicle with an eye toward the export market and it uses a greater number of commercial off-the-shelf automotive parts and other existing components to reduce overall cost and potential strains on logistics chains.
From our January story: “The two major variants the company has shown publicly, the KF31 and KF41, are relatively similar.
The KF41 has a larger overall configuration, though, with a weight of around 44 tons, almost 10 tons heavier than the KF31 and even bigger than the Puma in its base configuration.

Within these main versions, Rheinmetall has also offered a variety of mission-specialist Lynx vehicles. These include a mortar carrier, heavy fire support vehicle, self-propelled anti-aircraft gun with Skyranger 30 air defense turret, command and control vehicle, reconnaissance vehicle, recovery vehicle, and ambulance. Any of these could also be attractive to Ukraine, with a common platform offering logistics advantages as well as economies of scale.”
The Skyranger 30 variant is fully optimized for air defense and includes its own radar and short-range missile systems, but lacks the flexibility of the Lance 30 equipped variant like Ukraine uses.
Rheinmetall clearly sees a market for a new-generation infantry fighting vehicle, optimized for export, to challenge more established designs like the aforementioned Bradley and CV90.

Back to the U.S. Army’s involvement with Lynx, under the Army’s XM-30 program to replace the Bradley, previously known as the Optionally Manned Fighting Vehicle (OMFV), American Rheinmetall Vehicles and General Dynamics Land Systems are each building a prototype. Two previous efforts to replace the Bradley — the Future Combat System (FCS) program and the Ground Combat Vehicle (GCV) program — were cancelled.

Given the ubiquity of aerial surveillance drones in Ukraine, it may not take long before we see the Lynx in action. Then a better picture will emerge of how it performs against drones as well as in maneuver warfare.

items.titel: Ford in talks with the Pentagon to supply military vehicles

absaetze.t: Ford said on Tuesday it has held talks with the Pentagon about supplying military vehicles and other defense products to the U.S. military, as legacy automakers seek a share of fast-rising defense spending amid tough competition in the auto sector.

A Ford spokesperson said the discussions were focused on supplying highly capable military vehicles and working with U.S.-based space systems contractor Revolution Space to build advanced satellites. Ford had announced on Monday a minority investment in Revolution Space.

The Wall Street Journal first reported earlier in the day that the Pentagon was in talks with General Motors, Ford and other manufacturers to help mass-produce military drones by supplying parts including actuators, engines, sensors and lidar to drone companies.

“The Department of War is actively partnering with domestic manufacturers, suppliers, and emerging tech firms to build a resilient, high-capacity industrial base that accelerates the production, deployment, and long-term sustainment of next-generation unmanned and autonomous systems,” a Pentagon official told Reuters.
Detroit’s automakers have a long history of turning mass production capabilities toward military needs, having converted factories during World War II to build tanks, jet engines and trucks.

According to the Journal’s report, GM is weighing whether to manufacture drone motors, while U.S. defense officials have met with executives at Canadian auto parts maker Magna International and other manufacturing firms, some outside the auto industry.

GM has been most interested in getting involved with military projects at the request of high-ranking defense officials, the Journal said, adding that the automaker was in talks with RTX and L3Harris on a similar deal.

GM declined to comment on the report, but said in an emailed statement that its Defense unit has extensive capabilities and scale, and that it has “demonstrated our commitment to reinforce the U.S. defense-industrial base and help address critical needs.”
Magna said it had nothing to add with regard to the report.

items.titel: Have the US midterms brought an end to ‘nasty’ politics?
items.anriss: In the run-up to the US midterm elections earlier this month, voters in Texas saw their aspiring Democratic senator, James Talarico, adopt a bewildering array of personas. One Republican campaign ad showed him wearing a Julie Andrews-style …

absaetze.t: Affairs
November 25, 2026
4 Min Read
Across the country, candidates who ran political attack ads mostly lost their races. Does this signal a permanent move towards ‘nice’ politics or merely a temporary shift to it?

In the run-up to the US midterm elections earlier this month, voters in Texas saw their aspiring Democratic senator, James Talarico, adopt a bewildering array of personas. One Republican campaign ad showed him wearing a Julie Andrews-style apron dress, singing about transgender children to the tune of “My Favourite Things”. In another, he was reading aloud from the “King James Talarico Bible” and defacing it with sketches of himself.

While these ads were created by AI image generators, the tone of the attacks in the real world was downright unpleasant. Republicans pulled out all the stops to try and hang onto power in the once reliably red Lone Star State. The party threw at least $274m (€245m) at ads in the Texas Senate race but to no avail. Talarico beat Trump-approved Republican candidate Ken Paxton and handed the Democratic Party its first Senate win in the state since 1988.

The pattern repeated across the US: where the Republicans launched attack ads against their Democratic opponents, they tended to lose. In the 2024 presidential election, Republicans flooded swing states with ads that read “Kamala is for they/them, President Trump is for you”: a divisive message credited with encapsulating the voter mood at the time and helping to propel Trump to victory. This year, however, personal attacks and anti-trans lines fell flat, which raises the question: is this the end of nasty political ads in the US?

“Many of [the Democratic candidates] were quite conciliatory, trying not to talk about the divisive cultural issues and instead sticking to the bread and butter, the cost of living,” says Travis Ridout, co-director of the nonpartisan Wesleyan Media Project, which tracks political ads. “It was a different, probably smarter tone that Democrats took this year.”

A post-election poll commissioned by LGBTQ+ media advocacy group Glaad found that 56 per cent percent of surveyed voters thought that candidates used anti-trans rhetoric to divide and distract from important issues such as the economy. Data collected a few weeks before the elections by Scripps News found that more than three-quarters of voters said there should be rules around how AI is used in politics.

Tapping into suspicion of AI and data centres turned out to be an election-winning tactic for the Democrats. Voters didn’t want to spend time deciphering whether or not a post on social media was real. And authenticity was a selling point for many winning Democratic candidates: some Talarico ads signed off with the phrase, “made by humans, not AI”.

The most talked-about attack ad of the election cycle came from Ohio Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy. His campaign aired a real clip of his opponent’s estranged mother in which she accused her daughter, Amy Acton, of being a “liar”.

Acton beat Ramaswamy by a comfortable margin. A Yougov poll released shortly before the elections showed that 64 per cent of voters disapproved of the ad when they knew the full history: authorities removed Acton from her mother’s custody when she was 12 after she said that she was sexually abused by her stepfather.

2028 presidential hopefuls might be taking note. JD Vance has softened his tone in some appearances and stacked his social media with images of his young family, though not before misreading the room at a pre-election event where he told Republicans to “stop whining” about Ramaswamy’s ad.

But two years is a long time in politics and the mood could shift again before 2028. While there was a general weariness with the shouty, aggressive brand of politics this election cycle, that doesn’t mean that Americans will have the same appetite next time around. Whether they are nice or nasty, successful strategies tap into the mood of the moment, which can swing wildly from one election cycle to the next.

Personal attacks are as old as US politics, says former campaign strategist Peter Loge, citing the 1796 and 1800 John Adams-Thomas Jefferson races, which included fat-shaming slurs and claims that one candidate was a hermaphrodite. “There’s an old joke that if your antique British sports car stops leaking oil, it’s out of oil,” says Loge, now an associate professor of media and public affairs at George Washington University. “When American politics stops being nasty, politics won’t matter anymore.”

items.titel: Grand Theft Auto VI takes over Miami, including its art destinations
items.anriss: Rockstar Games collaborated with the Wynwood Walls museum ahead of the blockbuster game's release, and has replicated (but renamed) the Pérez, Bass and Wolfsonian museums inside the game

absaetze.t: Ahead of Art Basel Miami Beach, a massive marketing campaign for the blockbuster video game Grand Theft Auto (GTA) VI has transformed Miami—and the city’s art scene is coming along for the joyride.

On 13 October, the street art-focused Wynwood Walls museum unveiled a collaboration with the game’s developer Rockstar Games, inviting ten artists to create GTA-themed murals in and around the museum property. The museum also announced the partnership would include merchandising and free admission for all Miami-Dade County residents until the end of 2028, reversing a pandemic-era policy that saw tickets sold at the attraction for the first time.

The art-centric campaign is part of a massive marketing push around the game, which was released globally on 19 November to universal critical acclaim. Set in a satirical version of Miami called “Vice City”, the game world is an incredibly detailed virtual replica of the real city and the surrounding state of Florida (“Leonida”), complete with areas such as “Stockyard” replicating Wynwood with its street art and graffiti culture.

Demonstrating an extreme dedication to realism, Rockstar has even painstakingly replicated and renamed local landmarks such as the nightclub Club Space (“The Vault”), the beloved regional casual dining chain Flanagan’s (“Uncle Jack’s) and local art institutions such as the Pérez Art Museum Miami ("Future Leonida Art Museum", or "Flam") and the Wolfsonian–Florida International University design museum ("Hicksonian Museum of Art and Design"). Miami Beach’s Bass Museum of Art (“Vice City Museum of Art”) had its iconic Ugo Rondinone sculpture Miami Mountain (2016) turned into a monumental stack of emojis inside the game. (Unfortunately the current exhibition at the "Vice City Museum of Art", Karl Bergstrom: Diaspora, cannot be visited as the building is not currently accessible within gameplay.)

According to Jessica Goldman Srebnick, the Wynwood Walls museum’s chief executive and curator, Rockstar commissioned in-game murals from around 50 artists, many of whom have exhibited at the museum before. When the developer approached the museum to suggest a collaboration, it was a no-brainer. “Street art and gaming have a lot of shared cultural DNA, and they’ve influenced each other,” she says. The game’s creators “share our commitment to creativity, to supporting artists. They share our commitment and deep appreciation for the city of Miami. And I’m just really grateful that they are supporting something that provides more access to the arts.”

The murals in Wynwood, which will be on display until 1 January 2027, are similar to those featured in the game itself. A mural by the artist Queen Andrea, for instance, reads “Welcome to Vice City” in a curvy, neon-like font, while another by Ron English features a design with grenades in the shape of lightbulbs and the slogan: “There’s nothing more dangerous than a good idea.”

The project, as well as GTA’s larger presence in the city, has not been without controversy. The local newspaper Miami New Times reported on 10 November that one of the GTA murals had covered up a piece by the late artist Alex “Rect” Reyes, who finished the work shortly before his death in 2022. The wall had been considered a memorial by Reyes’s family and friends, who say they were not informed about its replacement. Goldman Global Arts, which owns the wall and museum, said in a statement to the New Times that it had offered Reyes’s crew a different wall to make amends.

Meanwhile, a joint partnership with Miami-Dade County and the Miami Heat professional basketball team has resulted in everything from player uniforms to the Kaseya Center arena in Downtown Miami being rebranded with “Vice City”. Massive crowds turned out for a Heat game on 18 November, the eve of the GTA VI’s release, to purchase custom merchandise that was only available at the arena. The total package, which includes lighting and signage inspired by the game at Miami International Airport and PortMiami, is valued at $3.9m according to a press release from the county government. Some officials have expressed alarm at the collaboration, with one county commissioner worried that the game is “depicting Miami like a murder capital”, according to the Miami Herald.
As for the benefits for the local art scene, perhaps gamers who visit GTA VI’s virtual “Vice City Museum of Art” will be inspired to seek out the Bass on their next visit to Miami Beach.

items.titel: Why you should be reading Helen Garner (and where to start).
items.anriss: Last week, The Paris Review announced the winners of its annual literary awards. In 2027, Australian author Helen Garner will be feted with the Hadada, a prize that recognizes a writer’s lifelong literary contributions. I am here as an …

absaetze.t: Last week, The Paris Review announced the winners of its annual literary awards. In 2027, Australian author Helen Garner will be feted with the Hadada, a prize that recognizes a writer’s lifelong literary contributions. I am here as an independent body to hype this choice.

Garner—a novelist, journalist, and diarist—writes big-hearted heroines who are often on the edge of a crisis. Her other fans include Lauren Groff, Lily King, Rumaan Alam, and Ben Lerner, but we are legion. Why, you ask?

In a recent piece for The Guardian, Emma Brockes also praised Garner’s “ability to combine insight and erudition of the highest literary order with a style that is at times comically down to earth.” And it’s true—that earthiness is what makes her work indelible. But it’s also just the tip of an iceberg.
Here are three of Garner’s best known books (and why you should make like the Parisians and pick them up, stat).

Monkey Grip, Garner’s 1977 debut, sent a shockwave through Australia. This novel chronicles a woman’s doomed-from-the-jump situationship with a heroin addict who charms her intermittently as they orbit a communal living situation.
A little like Susie Boyt’s sleeper hit, Loved and Missed, this book beautifully captures the recurring heartbreak involved in loving an addict. But it’s never saccharine, or sanctimonious.

Following a bohemian Melbourne milieu that echoes the author’s own set at the time, Garner’s non-judgmental portrait of freewheeling radicals brought out the moralizers on publication. Nora, our heroine, ruffled feathers for depicting ambivalent parenthood administered with a very loose latchkey. All adults in this book are libidinally motivated. Drugs and sex are world-structuring forces.

But what’s most exciting is how naked the prose is about all of that want. In Garner’s matter-of-fact voice, Nora’s thirst for the grifting Javo is rendered tender, abject, holy, and pathetic by turns. She feels like a real and vulnerable person with a mighty human flaw. The best kind of protagonist.

My favorite of Garner’s novels is The Children’s Bach. Another tale of domestic upheaval ignited by a charismatic chaos agent, this book traces the happily partnered Athena Fox’s infatuation with a blast from the past. Against reason, she leaves her partner and two small children for… a rock star.
What follows is a little predictable, but as with Monkey Grip the pleasure is in experiencing that slow road to ruin. (Or is it ecstasy?)
The third person POV serves this book, which manages to texturize everyone affected by Athena’s choices. She feels like a modern Nora, in the Ibsen sense.

The Spare Room is a cool, slim, spiky book. I find this Garner still gnaws at me. Following two semi-estranged old friends who fall back together when one seeks harbor following a terminal diagnosis, this novel depicts the unpleasant side of caretaking and the indignity of illness.
This book asks some truly itchy questions. Such as, what do you do when your patient is delusional—and/or, you want them out of your house?

As in the other novels, our protagonist chafes against conventionality and obligatory mutual obligation. And her extreme honesty hits you like a glass of cold water. As always, there’s a nakedness to a Garner subject. She doesn’t flinch from depicting those ugly emotions or unwanted thoughts.
In a review for the Times, Daphne Merkin once compared Garner to other “laconic and wayward,” ladies who specialize in the “art of artlessness, like Jean Rhys, Jane Bowles and Paula Fox.”
I agree with wayward, but I think that artful eye is in a class all its own. Do yourself a favor and join the Helen hive. Today.

items.titel: Here’s the shortlist for the first-ever Children’s Booker Prize.
items.anriss: Today, the Booker Prize Foundation announced the “Great Eight” shortlist of titles for inaugural Children’s Booker Prize, which will be awarded annually beginning in 2027. The Children’s Booker is the latest off-shoot of the prestigious …

absaetze.t: Today, the Booker Prize Foundation announced the “Great Eight” shortlist of titles for inaugural Children’s Booker Prize, which will be awarded annually beginning in 2027. The Children’s Booker is the latest off-shoot of the prestigious Booker Prize (most recently awarded to M. John Harrison’s The End of Everything) and celebrates fiction for eight- to 12-year-olds, written in or translated into English and published in the UK or Ireland. The winner will take home £50,000 and the Booker Foundation will be donating at least 30,000 copies of the shortlisted books to children across the United Kingdom and Ireland.

“Any of these books stands comparison with any adult book, whatever the category, on its own terms,” said Frank Cottrell-Boyce, Chair of the Children’s Booker Prize 2027 judges, in the shortlist announcement. He, along with fellow judges Sanchita Basu De Sarkar and Lolly Adefope, narrowed down the shortlist from 89 submissions and will be joined for the final decision by four young people: Ibrahim (12), Lainey (12), Luna (8), and Myla (11).
Here’s the shortlist:
Guy Bass, illustrated by David Roberts, The Worst Thing That Could Possibly Happen
Catherine Bruton, Tadpole Summer
Eoin Colfer and Andrew Donkin, illustrated by Giovanni Rigano, War
Iqbal Hussain, The Night I Borrowed Time
Liz Hyder, illustrated by Tom de Freston, The Teller of Tall Tales
Mikey Please, The Rambler’s Curse
Jessica Scott-Whyte, illustrated by Becka Moor, Séamus Almost Famous
Shaun Tan, Hometown
The winner will be announced in a ceremony on February 2, 2027.
